title: 15 additional small fixes
lede: Read-path correctness, safer exports, and navigation recovery. No layout redesign, schema migration, or production mutation.

sections.heading: Evidence boundaries
sections.note: Behavioral review only. No authenticated product screenshot or matched visual baseline was captured. Regression tests exercise real route wrappers with mocked identity/database boundaries and real helper functions; they do not prove a deployed browser session.

changes.was: Malformed dates reached Prisma; reversed windows looked like empty exports.
Audit, bookings, items and users downloads lacked an explicit no-store policy.
changes.now: All four CSV responses are private, no-store.

changes.was: The Collaborator role was missing from the export filter allowlist.
changes.now: Exports use the same role predicate as the directory.

changes.was: Unknown area values reached Prisma enum filters.
changes.now: Use the directory’s validated area predicate.

changes.was: Whitespace in location ids produced a different result from the directory.
changes.now: Trim location ids through the shared query builder.

changes.was: The route loaded every matching user synchronously.
changes.now: Read at most 5,001 rows, export 5,000, and mark truncation.

changes.was: Staff CSVs included fields hidden by the collaborator profile API.
changes.now: Staff CSVs retain name, role and title; private columns remain blank. Admin exports remain complete.

changes.was: Equal sort values had no unique tiebreaker.
changes.now: Append id ordering to every directory sort.

changes.was: Rows with equal timestamps could change order around the 5,000-row boundary.
changes.now: Audit and booking exports use createdAt plus id ordering.

changes.was: Leading whitespace bypassed client report formula protection.
A missing total-count header turned incomplete downloads into success messages.
changes.now: Both helpers retain warning severity without a total.

changes.was: JSON null leaked into failure copy as literal null.
changes.now: Null, arrays and primitives use the normal status-based fallback.

changes.was: Renaming the most recent item left the previous label stored.
changes.now: Update the label even when its URL is already first.

changes.was: Malformed JSON blocked every future recent-history write.
changes.now: The next visit rebuilds a valid cache.

changes.was: Filter synchronization replaced router/history metadata with null.
changes.now: Preserve the current history state while updating the URL.

verification: 132 focused tests pass across 12 files, including 35 new regression cases.
Nine helper regression cases failed against the original source and pass after the fixes.
TypeScript, lint, application build, codemap/docs verification and git diff --check pass.
No records were created, changed, exported from production, or deleted.

Headless Chromium passed four checks using the bundled source helpers: corrupt-storage recovery, first-entry rename, history-state preservation, and truncated-warning severity. The review page was rendered and inspected. This is isolated browser-helper evidence, not authenticated app proof.
notes: Authenticated browser interaction and production deployment remain unverified. No visual layout improvement is claimed.
The hidden-user test suite required a test-only no-preview cookie mock so kiosk visibility assertions could run without Next request context.
The source changes remain local and uncommitted.
